I am suprised with this game. I waited until it was on sale because it seemed risky to pay full price for 'far cry without guns'. It is actually really good. The player movements are more refined in some ways than even far cry 4, and you feel more agile. The forest environment is really beatiful, and the hunting in the primal setting actually fits with the game, whereas in far cry 3/4 it seems out of place to me. Shooting with the bow takes more skill than guns because you have to lead and elevate, and deal with less ammo and slower rate of fire. The survival mode is really fun. Definitely a risk worth taking for Ubisoft; a much more interesting twist on a franchise than others such as assassins creed have to offer. Many of the things you do in regular far cry actually make more sense in a primitive time period. Also really nice to have a day/night cycle. On survival expert mode, primal is more immersive to me; gotten so used to far cry even on hard that it seems easy by comparison.

Call of Duty Ghosts is (in my opinion) a re-make of Modern Warfare 2. The only new feature I find interesting was the sniper scope. I feel this is more of a downgrade from Black Ops 2, the previous title. They attempted to make it more realistic like Battlefield, but I liked the non-realism that was given in Black Ops 2. I do not recommend buying this. In fact, you should just buy Black Ops 2 with the money that you saved towards this game, or wait for the upcoming one made by Treyarch. Infinity Ward also had terrible quality and support for PC players in comparison to the PS3, PS4, Xbox360 and Xbox One. There are a lot less players on the PC version of Ghosts than others.

Killer Is Dead is a very bloody action/slasher game. You play a half cyborg/half samurai sword fighter. (It's a bit like 'Devil May Cry') Using a comic book style cinematics to tell a story, you run around in rooms fighting off cybornetic monsters. You get paid with gems, which help you upgrade your character, and money. Each time you complete a room or chapter, you are given a rating on how you did and money based on how well you performed.  Overall a fun game to play. Warning, it not 'Alt-Tab' safe, At least not for me.

Do the cutscenes play? Nope. Are there some annoying bugs that make it difficult to play on modern systems? Yep. Is it better than any modern game released? Yes. You take ANY level in this game, nevermind The Sword and Banford's Mansion, and you have an entire game that is better than most modern releases full games today. It's that simple. Stealth, detection of your presence, your awareness of your visibility to your opponents, your realization of levels of detection by voice cues and whether you have a chance of just staying in the shadows all make this games one of the MOST INTENSE battles you will EVER face without ever firing a single shot. You don't fire fight in this game. Two blows from a Hammer's hammer and you are done. No 200% armor, no superhealth, no quad damage, no invulnerability. It's just you; a mace, a few arrows filled with water and moss and hopefully a flash bomb or two. It doesn't get more real than this game and you can feel the love and care in every level

I played for like 7 minutes and that was enough to decide I was uninstalling it. Bought it on sale, so no harm done. As for why I don't like it I will start by saying that I understand its a low budget game and it will not have quite the polish of other games. But I just could not get into it. It looks good in stills but the character animations are where it falls apart. Just a few extra key frames would smooth things out and look kinda nice. Currently it looks like someone's first attempt at a flash animation. Also, I can kinda put up with the storyboard style cut scenes, but the execution in this game is mediocre at best.  I cannot comment on the story, however, or much of the gameplay mechanics as all I did was read through a cut scene, run forward, fight two dudes, and turn off the game.

It's a good game, but I must confess I did get bored time to time. I like the consequence rule, and it makes it feel like a RPG made funny. Some of the characters you meet is detailed good and you grow attached to them. The best part of this game is still not the gameplay. It's the music. The music makes this game.   Gameplay: 6/10  Music/Sounds: 10/10  Story: 7/10   Can't remember how many of the hours I have played this game have been spent just standing still listen to the music. 'the pub song ('sans.)' and 'spider dance' is just two of the best songs in the game.

This game is without a doubt one of the best games I have ever played. There are hours of fun, whether this be side campaign missions, side missions, rampages, playing The Multiplayer Mod completing locations, races, or exploring. The whole game is highly replayable, especially the thrilling campaign missions. Most of the side mission locations are extremely well thought out and unique, as well as fun to explore. The scenery is exemplary, better than most games today. I hear a lot of people complaining about bugs. In my 69 hours as of writing this game I have encountered one bug in which I rappled into a wall, forcing me to respawn. If you count cars bouncing uncontrolably as a bug I have encountered that too. However, neither of these take away from the gameplay. Overall, this game is absolutely perfect for anyone who likes third person shooters, explosions, or open world games. This game is the perfect game to buy on sale since without a doubt you will get your money's worth.

Nostalgia! This game was obviously developed to mimic many of the old school top-down shooters from the 1997-2001 period. This game is cheesy, incoherrnet, unforgiving and heaps of fun. Unique characters, retro graphics with interesting contrast and use of light, simple leveling system, 90's techno music, ♥♥♥♥ loads of cool guns and an absolute ton of zombies to mow down. Campaign took me just under 5 hours, and I'm still getting some fun out of survival mode. If you can appreciate the retro style then this is a great game to kill some time on.

If you buy this game, make sure to download the 2.36 beta patch and the reign of the ancients mod from the paradox forums. It makes the game a hundred times better.  Also, if you're having trouble installing the mod on windows 10 then follow Thypus's installation instructions instead.  1 Have a clean install of the game 2 copy the province_texture folder on the map/cache folder and stick it in the desktop for example 3 patch to 2.36b in the rome folder 4 install the mod in the mod folder 5 change the name of the cache folder (in map folder) to cache_vanilla 6 create a new folder named cache in map folder and then stick inside the previous province_texture that you have copy in the desktop 7 then stick in the mod/map/cache folder the province_texture folder aswell  And if you have the problem which makes parts of the map blue in terrain view then do this:  'you have to follow Thypus's installation instructions and then replace everything in the rome/map/cache folder except the province terrain folder with everything (except the province terrain folder) thats in the mod/map/cache folder.'  All of that should only take ten minutes to setup at the most. (as long as you don't mess up) Hope this helped your decision!

This is a solid, pretty little shmup with nice beefy gun sounds and a hectic soundtrack. I like that for once it's not set in space. Here we're underwater fighting fish-robots!... okay. Points for bucking the trends anyway. One criticism is that the upgrade system was a little unintuitive at first, or at least it could have been explained better, but it is there and that's great. Perform better on a mission and you get better loot to upgrade or buy entirely new subs with.   Recommend for any shmup fans.

When I first heard of this game, I was extremley excited. I had heard great things about how well the story was put together and how the character development really sucks you in. After completing it, I was really disapointed. The game tells stories through picking up items and then a magical audio book plays where another character in the game tells a story. Now thats cool and all but Gone Home is not the first to use the consept and they did not do as good as a job as other games have. Bioshock did a way better job then Gone Home. ♥♥♥♥ the Fallouts did better jobs then Gone Home. I do have to admit that the story is intresting tho, could of been a lot better. Gone Home is not worth $20. I highly suggest either buying it during a steam sale (I did that) or torrenting it. If you torrent it and enjoy it, then go ahead and buy it. But I highly suggest torrenting it, it can be extremly disapointing.

Tried reloading a saved game and I returned with only 2 Ants out of about the 100 I had. It was hard for me to decide weither or not i would recommend it do to the issues I had today, But its a good time killer and you can always restart.

Wasted was a game I didn't really think was very special until I played it, resulting in many a late night running dungeons at high speed with several hangovers.  A fun game, almost a fallout style, mixed with the ability to get many skills without having to go down a tree, Wasted continues to consume my free time.  I wish the music played during loading screens, however, because I really enjoy the ingame radio and hate having to miss out on 5-10 second clips in the middle of each song.

This is a pretty good game. Even though the gameplay is a little bit slow in the beginning, It'll eventually be high management of resources and trying not to drown in debt. You have to realize that you're playing a game simulating farming, by nature It won't be crazy. But in the end, it's good fun to sit down and view your vast empire of farming glory. In my own opinion, this game was a good investment.

Horrible controls kill this game. I can get behind the concept, and the music is fitting, but the only supported inputs are the arrow keys. Even if you try to map a controller in the Unity options, the game ignores it.  Gameplay in a nutshell: you are glued to either the top or bottom of the screen, and need to pass through the gaps between letters in order to collect them to form the word shown at the bottom of the screen. Unfortunately you have very little time to react, and combine that with a tilting camera that makes it extra unclear where exactly your block is located compared to the upcoming letters, and this game becomes less about skill and more about luck.  This game either needs to get rid of the tilting camera, or give some kind of indication where exactly your cursor is, by a shadow or light in front perhaps. In its current state it only serves as a source of frustration.

Let me first start off by saying that though I have played through other RE games, it has not been a major staple of gaming life. That stated, this game is an interesting one. A Rainbow Six style shooter with not as many tactics involved. The game is best experienced with friends. The graphics aren't particularly great, but the game can have an interesting draw to it that I really can't explain. Each of the characters has some cool things that can be done, the weapons are interesting, as well as the special abilities.  All in all this game is far from perfect. But if you approach it with the mindset that this isn't your standard RE game, I think it has some interesting aspects to it.  I believe it is worth your time and consideration.

As with most games, when I saw dreamfall, I was a little wary. It isn't cheap but I decided to give it a chanse, mostly because I had watched the youtuber Cryaotic play the prequel, and because I am Norwegian... I was amazed. I have always loved a good story and this game sucked me right in. I sat for a long time, even with the easiest of decisions and wondered what impact it could have on the rest of the game.  The way Zoe and Kian moved compared to the enviroment was a little off from time to time, and I did get stuck alot since the game wants you to do one specific thing and you have no idea how, it can be a little annoying. But the rest weights up for this. The amazing story, which I can't wait to see the end of, well develouped characters with personality and independence unlike in any other game, and even easy decicions become hard. I'll say it is well worth it.  Great job Red thread!

Overall, very enjoyable game.   The theme, aesthetics, music, and sound design are all brilliant. Awesome futuristic guerrilla warfare vibe. From the cutscenes to the stylistic loading screens, this game is cool.  The gameplay feels very polished, with some clear improvements over the previous title, Enemy Unknown. Although, at the time of writing, there is still some room for improvements. I assume that some of the issues with line of sight, and general performance will get fixed. The loading times are long, that's a shame but acceptable, the maps are procedurally generated to an extend. The general performance is not very good though. For example there has been times where a really long mission has required me to exit the game, to clear up some memory from all the debris and corpses hogging the frames.  Despite all of this I've completed the game, and had a fun time with it. If you enjoy strategy with some randomness thrown in, and an excellent management layer on top, then this is the game for you.

So first of all, let me just say that Manyland has one of the nicest communities of any game I've ever played.  The amount of support I've recieved from the commuity alone is phenominal... And to hear positive things from people saying my creatons are good is really nice! The game itself is more of a tool than a game... Think of Little Big Planet, it's similar to that except the world in which you build is forever evolving as people add more to it.  You don't crteate levels as such, it's more like a platform where you create your own worlds and can make them into anything you want! Would I recommend this game? YES! It's quirky, fun and you can be whatever and make whatever you want!

Its such a bummer remedy abandoned this franchise. This game was so well written, and brought something new to the table. If you haven't played it yet it's definatly worth the cost. Every once and a while I go back to this game to experience again. It reminds me of when I was 11 playing RE2 for the first time. There's very few moments where you feel comfortable as the game always keeps you on your toes.   The idea they had for the sequels looked pretty awesome too, so if you can pick up American Nightmare you should, its short, but awesome in its own right.  I hope Remedy decides to come back and add more to this franchise.

Music: 2 great songs such as noel and yeul's theme (great at setting the sad mood within the game). The con is the horrible metal screaming while riding red chocobos.  Characters: 2 characters in your party and one monster are used. The characters were more 'real.'They showed more emotion and had more sides to them than the previous game. You can also choose what they say, aka humorous responses throughout the game.  Cinematic battles that you can interact with using quick time events that effect the battles after the scene.  Lots of side quests, areas, and replayability.   One large con is the amount of sidegames. They range in difficulty, but the vast amount in some areas make them tiring and frustrating.  10/10 would play again!!!!

I don't know if I've ever been addicted to a game as I have been for this one. It is simply BADmfnASS!! I have put hours into this game and I basically know the maps and I love every skirmish every check point and every kill. Todays shooters always focus on the 'ME' aspect and what I achieved, but never before I constantly want my buddies(insurgency community) to win along side me as a team. Each rifle has it's pwn weight and feel and it's perfectly balanced. The sounds of the game are awesome and it lets you immerse yourself in the match/conflict. It's real juice is the community itself. Communication and teamwork is key and if you buy this game, pls get a headset and mic, It is absolutely a blast to talk with teammates as you help each other achieve the objective.  So WTF are u still reading this, buy this well worth the full admission game. DO IT!! C'MON, DO IT NOW!!!

Absolutely one of the best games I've played in a long time. With a turn-based RPG style battle system similar to FFVII, a nice use of an array of buildable augmentation devices on weapons, and a rotating, large cast of characters that each have different strengths (depending on how you want to level them), this game is a pleasure to do battle in. Not only that, but it's visually spectacular, the soundtrack - while a little repetitive after 15 hours - is still absolutely beautiful, the kind of thing you could happily play in the background even if you weren't gaming. An interesting, in-depth story that felt like a true fairytale, and very smooth gameplay dynamics overall. Really enjoyed this one! Probably the best game I've played in years.

I would like to say this game had my interest sparked from the beginning of when the game was announced but I had only started investing into it about 3 weeks before the game came out. The game itself had very good marketing but thats about the best thing about the game.  Pros -Very Intriguing idea -Well marketed  Cons -Didn't fulfill the promises set out to make the game -Creatures are procedurally generated looking like the exact same as one on another planet while just having a small difference -Very little depth to the game itself and is very repetitive -Doesn't have any sort of way to enjoy with your friends as the game doesnt really have anything worth while showing -Game lacks proper optimization even though its not early access  Overall the game didn't do a very good job at fulfilling what it said was going to do and It lacked the gameplay to be considered a 60$ game.

Great campaign! really enjoyed it, I could actually follow exactly what was going on which in most COD games I simply cant follow whats happening. Black ops 3 was rubbish and this is great in comparasion. My favourite COD campaign since Modern wafare. Graphics are OK but after Gears 4, Battlefield 1 and Titanfall 2 just before it this is not quite as stunning as those games were. Great mix of Shooting and Jackal action, paced well and not overly crazy on futuristic powers. Great characters and perfomances. Zombies is the is as fun as last time. Cant speak for multi player as I dont play it ( sick of losing all the time )

Well Holy ♥♥♥♥! I bought this game one boring winter break with money from the holidays thinking 'Aw, what the hell? It's cheap and has pretty good reviews.' Turns out this game was much more fun (And difficult) Than i would have ever thought. The plot is fairly simple and easy to follow, but it's still there. I loved the music (especially the song that play's after the encounter in the mirror room.) and it changed on every floor of the tower, cycling through all sorts of various tunes and styles. The controls felt smooth (At least when playing as Yunica, I don't know about hugo) and it was especially nice to move around with dash/ double jump. But i think the best part of Ys:Origin is the boss fights. Most enemies will fight, and while their no pushovers, they go down pretty easy. But the boss's, damn are they angry. The one I remember giving me the most trouble was the end boss of the Guilty Fire segment. so many hours went in to beating that guy. but all of the boss's give trouble, keeping you in the heat of the action every time you think you've figured them out. This is the first game I've played in the YS series, and i had no trouble figuring out who went where and what was when, I Highly reccomend this game to people who enjoy quick, smooth combat and challenging bossfights with a wide varity of music!

Completing this game is in so far not possible as you can play it over and over again. The levels change each time, the encounters as well.  One time I met a skeleton with a violin (really scary sounding one) who asked me to take the curse from him... he was actually a nice guy... except for the, you know, trying to kill me part.  The game plays a whole lot like Super Smash Bros. which is great! Finally a game that picks up on the game machenics. Too bad there are only 3 buildable characters, the other once are set, but nice to play as well.   Took me about 4 hours for my first playthrough, since you have to start over again after too many mistakes... and always remember... being swapped to a soldier sucks... but nice to know he is always there.  Edit: You as FYI: Friendly fire sucks when playing with my mates.

State of Decay is a lot of fun if you're into zombie survival. I sure am. It's a fairly well balanced game, too, although I wish AI survivor companions knew enough to pull feral zombies off of me once in a while. Speaking of ferals, the game has a set of freak zombies that are extremely dangerous encountered with groups of normals. However, when encountered alone, they're much easier not because your survivors are overpowered (they're not) but because you learn their behavior patterns and can counter them effectively: The first time I combat-rolled away from a feral's tackle attempt before following up with a ground finisher for a one hit kill, I almost squealed with glee. It was very satisfying.  I liked the game. I just wish I could build my own survivors. That would be a lot of fun.

The Conquest mode in the beginning of the game is brilliant! Why haven't we seen a system like this before? It's always the other way around - player finishes the game and then the game reports on the consequences. In my opinion, alone this system is carrying this game to be one of the best games of 2016!  But the selling pitch for this game is that the player represents the evil in the world, but when I played it, it just feels realistic. The occupying foreign force will always be 'the evil force' no matter how nice or just it is. This game just makes me think about human nature, morality and what role mercy and compassion should/could play in war. Although it looks that way, it's not your standard heroic fantasy RPG where you slay dragons and save the kingdom. This game is dark, cruel and, most importantly, has a very clever way of handling choices and consequences.        2016: Nominated for the Steam “Villain Most In Need Of A Hug” Award

What an epic tale that was!   I thoroughly enjoyed every bit of this gorgeous, touching journey where you control two brothers on a quest to save their fathers life.   This game really must be played using a controller with two analouge sticks, as each stick controls one of the brothers simultaneously. Yup, your left/right brain parts are gonna have to get coordinated to make this work :)  The genre is adventure/platforming with a hint of puzzle.   It's quite short - took me 3 hours to complete the main story, but I got only 2 acheivements. None of the achievements are for completing anything related to the main story - you have to go exploring to find them. But those 3 hours are just pure concentrated fairytale goodness.   Everything looks and sounds fantastic.  A must play for anyone remotely into the genre - although it's not recommended for the youngest/most impressionable (My eyes got a wee bit misty for a split second at one point).  90%

I have this game on android and still enjoy it. That't why when I saw a very good sale on steam I bought it immediately. This game of Winter Wolves is good to spend some hours, therer are many choices and both female and male options and also career path. Personally, I play this because of female and I do like all of them (but I am only interesting in Juliet though).  Beside that, there is one thing I do not like. It is the way you have to choose only professional ending or romance ending. It would be more fun if the game allow my character can go through both in one play time, and it also makes more sense ( Why someone has good career means cannot has love...)

It's addicting but it's very easy to figure out a strategy that gets you plenty of fans. I played until I unlocked all the outfits and then stopped because it doesn't have a lot of variety. Even unlocking the photos by buying all the oufits for all the girls feels pointless because it's just the loading screen pictures so it doesn't feel like you're achieving anything. Kyu becomes extremely annoying very fast because there are certain tutorials you can't skip. Watching your fan counter go up at the end of the level is also annoying because you can't skip it. Some of the voices are clearly reused from HuniePop.  All in all it isn't a great game and sometimes comes across as a bit lazy or rushed. If you're like me and just want something to do with your hands while you listen to something else then it isn't too bad. But there are plenty of other simple games that don't take a lot of attention and can keep your attention for much longer. It isn't very expense so it isn't too much of a loss if you don't buy it. I just suggest spending your money somewhere else.

(25/3/2015) Bought this game few days ago, been play through quite awhile, i keep ramming into a lot of invisible collision or the badly build collision. Reaching lvl 67 is a problem, you need to pay a few DLCs which you only can access into the casino and unlcok some cars too, which i'm dissapointed there. Atari's website kinda a bit haywire. Only got 2 radios?? SERIOUSLY?  This game is fun when you cruising around the 2 island with your friend or some random player. This game is okay but not that great. I still surprise there still got people playing this game after already been few years.

It makes a great companion to producing You Tube vidoes or non-pro audio production when you need some fun voice effects. Some of the voice effects are very cheesy, but there are some winners in here that are useful when you need a distortion filter, echoes, some radio crackle, or some other on the fly effect. Some things don't work as well with other software (background noises cutting out over teamspeak when you are set to push-to-talk, the input volume level matters here), and I would recommend a powerful compuiter to avoid lag. Have another person listen to you and give honest feedback when customizing voices and effects, this is something that's hard to do by yourself. Worth the price? I'd say yes, because it pulls together ease-of-use, simplicity, a decent driver, instructions, with a bunch of options in one package.

The mechanics of Rogue Legacy are simple. You have a sword to slash, magic spells to use, and the occasional class ability. You travel through 4 areas of a pseudo-randomly generated castle fighting the many enemies and the occational mini and full bosses. Though the game may sound like a grind, and may even feel like it for the first few lives, you soon will become addicted to its rewarding and fun gameplay. The mechanics are greatly executed and the gameplay keeps interest over several playthroughs. Controls are spot on, but I would recommend using a gamepad if you have one. One more thing, if the normal game is not enough of a challenge for you, the remix bosses will make you cry.

This is the first game in a while that has kept my interest this long, Parkour is so much fun once you get the hang of it, combat is a blast, side quests are more like fetch quests but are still loads of fun. The story is pretty meh around the board. I felt little obligation to be 'The Hero of Harran'. Besides that this game has a few other minor yet frustrating weak points. The acheivement system is still broken (Patch 1.5). It's annoying especially in the late game (which while still fun to goof around) there isn't much point in playing anymore. It's been about a month and a half since release and it feels like nothing has been done for it. People have had success by restarting their games but i honestly feel like I shouldn't have to jump through hoops for a basic element of all games to work. While this is currently an annoyance to me now I still have to give techland credit for expanding a genre thats getting oversaturated with a game that truly stands above the rest

Nah.  To be fair, it had some pretty neat ideas here and there but they were only surface level deep. The story is very uninspired and predictable which may be the fault of the source material which I'm not familiar with because I ain't got nothin in life by readin and I aint about to start. The world seems very 'trying-to-be-gritty' for lack of a better term. Yeah we get it Darkness II ripping out a man's heart = so edgy, you're a real game now. Maybe if the game didn't try to play it so straight and played the events with more levity I could have enjoyed the story more but I guess the source material doesn't allow for that. The gameplay is serviceable and even challenging a times but it really feels by the numbers, no clever enemy AI, no emergent game systems, bad fps boss battles, and very straightforward level design. So when there are areas that are challenging it comes off as cheap rather than a failure in learning the games systems. There's a few areas where the cell shaded art style really creates some cool looking environments but there are just as many uninspired ones.   I get that it is trying to do an arcade shooter but frankly there are better examples of this, and with better storytelling too. See Call of Juarez: Gunslinger or the new Shadow Warrior reboot. Those are far better games to play.

Cthulhu Saves The World is a 16-bit old school traditional console style role playing game. The game has been dated by over 20 years, but still is fun for those who appreciate the older generation style. The game's battle system is intuitive and encourages magic point management. The story is linear, and took me about 8 hours with in depth exploration on my first run. I do encourage playing it on the hardest setting for the most fun, and because the normal setting is a bit easy for the seasoned adventurer. The replay value is low, as the story is a bit bland for a linear game. Overall, it was a fun old school romp with a bit of humor and micromanagement, but I'm not going to pick it up again anytime soon. If you enjoy it, make sure to play Breath Of Death VII, written by the same designer.

Great idea for a game. In fact I was enjoying myself despite having to wait forever each time for my turn again. Until I realized only three cards, and rarely having attack cards which you need drop is a bad thing. Aka round 1-2. It's not fun if you can't attack and kill everything. I mean yeah let them gain up on me give me a good chance to die, that I don't mind. Being cornered where I can't even hit back and am stuck just sitting there or quitting. That tends to ruin a good game. It's kind of heart breaking really I was hoping for a semi relaxing yet still make you think game. Maybe after a few touch ups? But for now I can't seem to recommend it.

It has branching paths, which do lead to different choices and, possibly, endings, which is a good design choice. I feel like its too bloated, with non-relevant information. In the beginning of the game, some words are highlited in blue, which tell you about various things in the game. But the game shouldn't have to spell out your life through these blue links, but rather, let you experience them when those moments come up in the game. Also, while the different choices are a good touch, sometimes, almost all of my multiple choices are crossed out, so I'm only able to choose one option. This means I can't get any other endings (if there are any.) I don't really reccomend it, because its only an okay-written game, and nothing groundbreaking like articles made it out to be upon its release.

If you like your games to be super repetitive and lacking in atmosphere, then this is for you. It's much like being caught in one of thoe Maize Mazes in the countryside in summer. At first they are ok but it soon wears off as you go around and around, looking at the same thing, over and over. Yet, with Daylight we get a story, which isn't much. I played this for about an 40 mins and basically I couldn't take anymore. The graphics are really poor, despite having everything set on max and having a good system to run it on. I was hoping that given that this was one of the firsr games to use the new engine we would see something different, but instead it's really rather poor. Granted the game is cheap, but seriously, there are much better games on Steam and elsewhere that deserve your money. Polygon rated this as a 5 and I thought that perhaps they were being harsh. In reality, they were being generous. This is quite easily one of the worst games I've played of this genre, come to think of it, of any genre.

My first FPS experience on PC: Having limited myself to strategy and rpg games now seems like a mistake. I should have been playing everything on PC from day one. From the menu, I was blown away by the graphics and totally immeresed in the world and I wanted to see everything. Nothing on console compares to the experience that this brings to the table. The world is colorful and immersive and the control scheme is a thing of beauty once you die 20 times on hard and master it. I'm still early in, but I can see that the story is turning out to be better than expected; I was quite taken by the fact that the 'religious zelotry' that was always mentioned in previews for this game went well beyond that and covered social issues that predominated that time. For any, gaming, history buffs this is truly a treat in itself. So even though I'm a year late, and if you are too, lace 'em up and join the fray. There's a great world waiting on you.

This game has a really beautiful and unique atmosphere, and does a great job world-building for such a short game. There aren't any opportunities to rebattle monsters [until late in the game], but it does feature three different endings. The plot and writing are great, though I might find the endings a little anticlimatic (as in, what happens to the worlds after the events of the endings occur? There's no way to know). But the designs? Great. And the music is hauntingly beautiful, absolutely my favorite part of the game [and that's a rare thing for me]. Not to mention the battle system, which I think is incredibly unique regarding fusion spells, though I'm sure other, more experienced gamers could name a few.  9/10 would highly recommend for anyone who wants a quick little RPG with surprising and incredible depth to its story.

Mount and Blade: Warband is a lovely game which you should buy.... right now! It is a combination of different genres. It has some RPG elements because you create your own unique character and can level up/train various skills like one handed, shield, bows, trading and many more. It is also a strategy game because you build your own army out of a great amount of different units. It has some simulation aspects because you can become a lord and manage your castle(s) and town(s), your relations with other lords or even create your own faction. But the main reason why I played so many hours of this game is that there is a good amounts of mods which can complete overhaul your game. One mod in particular (Prophesy of Pendor a.k.a. POP) has drawn me in by it's great mechanics and lore. A must buy for anyone who loves strategy games with a good amount of RPG elements in it!

Star Conflict is a really fun little game.   I'm not a 'heavy duty gamer', but this game is just cool and fun. The controls are relatively simple, and the gameplay is fluid and responsive. My computer couldn't quite handle the full graphics settings, but even with the graphics dialed down a bit the game is still gorgeous.  The ships remind me of something out of Wing Commander, and the fluid movement reminds me of old favourite games like Descent. PVP games can take a few minutes to queue up, but they're well worth it. Win or lose, the game is fun and challenging.. and fast paced for exactly the 'quick in, quick out' game play I was looking for.  If you're looking for a fun game you can play for an hour or so, and get in a few pick-up matches, and you like space shooters.. then this one really is fantastic. And really, you can't beat the price!

Yeah, kill an enemy with bare hands, headshot or using enviromental explosions. If you liked Bulletstorm and its XP counting, you will find it here too.  The story doesn't interrupt playing, it's rather linear and easy to foreseen. Yet, it nicely explains the river of warriors to fight with.  One part I wish to be improved are boss-fights. In theory they were supposed to be challenging of some kind. But the AI makes bosses do all the time the same actions... while on upper levels, with all improvements to the basic pistol (where ammo never finishes) kill is made SOOOO easy!

Batman Arkham Kight has some well documented techincal problems on PC, however I seem to be one of the few people who has not experienced anything game breaking. Yes, the game is locked at 30fps and I have not gone into my files to change that cap. I have not experienced any crashes or bugs or anything game breaking.   I am a huge fan of the Batman Arkham fan. I still believe the first game, Asylum is one of the best games of all time. Batman Arkham Knight is another solid outing in this series, and a thilling conclusion to this trilogy. It is dark and twisted and as the player you are right there with Batman to experience every insane thing that happens on this frightening night.  I'm sorry to hear about all the techincal issues with the game, but beyond that this is a fun and engaging Batman game. It's not as good as the first game for me, but there are definitely some moments that are just as memorable. Do this give this game a shot after it's been patched up some more.

Compared to the original, it's a lot more linear and about story rather than keeping you scared at all times. The story can be quite confusing but overall the writing is rather good. If you like linear stories, by all means go for it, but if you're looking for a more openworld horror-game this might not be for you.

The best game I have ever played in twenty years of computer gaming, bar none (and I have played a LOT of games). Eight years on I can still recall how profoundly that game gripped me, and I am not an overly emotional person. You will care about the characters, you will be moved, you will make choices that tell you more about yourself. It sounds trite, I know, but it really is that good. If only someone would make more of these...insightful, intelligent, devastatingly creative. Fallout is the only RPG to come close. A word of warning: You MUST read all the text, explore all the dialogue options, if you are to gain the most from the game. A decent intelligence and wisdom score is recommended.....although so is a decent score in everything else....the game does the best job of making usually superflous statistics genuinely useful that I have ever seen. Still very much worth playing.

This a big step backwards from GRID 2. While it looks and plays much the same there is really no customisation options at all. Your not creating your on team here so theres no personalised livery's, no cars to be won or earned just driving so basically all your experience earns you is access to more races. Pick you sponser, drive the tracks, repeat. This may be a more accurate simulation of the 'world of professional Motorsport' but for me it lacks anything to motivate me to continue.  That said If your into racers you may enjoy it. it is a well made racing sim but if your more of a casual racer your probably going to find this a bit dull.

A Promising Start  Think LA Noire meets Sin City meets The Wolf Among Us. This game takes the best elements from each of those titles. The crime scene investigation and strong plot (LA Noire), the surreal tone and intuitive combat (Wolf Among Us), and the graphic novel art style (Sin City). Throw in a demonic cult stealing children and keeping them in a dungeon, and you've got one hell of an experience.  The plot has got me hooked and, if the writers can keep this up, this game could well go on to be an all time classic.   This game deserves way more publicity than it has received.

This game is fun, but there are a few things I didn't like about it. If this game is currently on sale, ignore my cons and buy it! It's a good game to pick up cheap!  PROS: Challenging Rogue-Like Cheap fun A unique game for a familiar genre Good music (see cons) Pleasant art style Can run on a potato without being ugly  CONS: The music doesn't play constantly throughout the game The story makes no sense Enemies are too predictable Enemies come in little variety OMG the turrets are OP Turrets can only be killed with bombs Bombs are rare If I turret is close to the next level door and you have no bombs, you can't proceed Map is too straight forward  Gunplay is unsatisfying  7/10 solid game, but I'd recommend buying it on sale.  EDIT: after playing more, I realized that the turrets can be killed if you shoot their battery. My bad. Turrets still are annoying little buggers though.

I first played this game about 2 years ago on the Xbox 360. I stopped playing and just never got into it. I thought the learning curve was just too steep. I thought the game just had cheap deaths for the sake of it.   Then I seriously started playing the game again on Steam about 2 months ago. I haven't been able to stop playing since. It's definitely rewarding, just prepare to die. And you learn from each death. Now I can do all of Blighttown and not die once (unless you get invaded). It's my favorite game of 2014 and it's from 2011.   There are prettier looking games out there. But this game has the perfect balance of gameplay that rewards players for being smart, i.e. patience and observation, trial and error. 10/10  Praise the Sun!

Definitely my game of the year.  This game features amazing gameplay that keeps you hooked and wanting to play. Melee combat is tactical and visceral, requiring quick thinking to avoid being taken down by hordes, especially in the beginning of the game.  The night brings real fear as you're chased through the streets by shrieking parkour zombies.  The story, while not the world's most amazing, is good enough to keep you interested throughout the game.  Graphically, the game is AMAZING. Beautiful scenery and gruesome zombies, the detail on everything is excellent, especially after the graphical fix they implemented.  Honestly, if you pass on this game, you're missing out on a great experience. It's so good I bought it for PS4 and decided to buy it again on PC because I didn't have anyone to play it with on the PS4. Season pass on both.

'You think you'll get your own squad after what happened last night?' - heard way too many times.   Best stealth game I've played so far. Really fun to go through the game learning the story while creeping up to people and choking them to sleep. Definitely gonna try another run of the game to try out the different ways the game can end up.  The downside to stealth games would have to be the dumb enemies. Right now, pretty much all games can't do it, but it's probably because it would be more fun that way, so it can't be helped.  Would definitely recommend.  Edit: Finished the game (including DLCs) 3 times over already. The challenges of not alerting/killing made me play it over and over :P

This game is great. It's like playing WORMS in multiplayer in medieval times. Castle construction, castle sieges and castle destruction. If that isn't enough, grab a drill dig underground all the way to the enemies’ base! Or grab a giant keg bomb and suicide yourself to destroy enemy fortifications and let your teammates in. The enemy is at your gates? Construct a ballista or a catapult and crush them into pieces! Heck, there is even naval warfare! Enemy built a wall in the middle of the ocean and you cannot get through? Get a giant ship and wreck it pieces and everything on its way!  This game inspires creativity and requires great teamwork. It is buggy, but its worth a try and I definitely do love it!
